subject: Model affinity exemption & geo lock for TruMed pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Willoughby <sara.willoughby@trumed.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model affinity exemption & geo lock for TruMed pilot

Hi team —

Quick background: TruMed is kicking off a month-long pilot for conversational triage where they require two things for their pilot environment: (1) model affinity to an audited, quantized variant (they want us to funnel their traffic to model-v2-q4_0 and not fall back to multi-model autoscale variants), and (2) a strict US-region lock (no routing to eu/apac). They flagged these as non-negotiable for PHI-adjacent workloads in the pilot.

They've attached their security checklist (TruMed_Security_Req.pdf) and a mapping of endpoint usage (pilot-mapping-v1.xlsx). Questions for product/security/ops:
- Can we carve an exemption that pins their route to a specific model variant when capacity exists, but also provides a documented fallback policy for our side if that variant is unhealthy? TruMed wants "no fallback" in contract language, but legal/ops want some fail-safe.
- Operationally, what would it take to ensure routing never leaves the US region (VPC + AZ constraints)?
- If we agree to an "affinity" mode, what monitoring/alerting and SLA adjustments do we need to request from TruMed?

Requesting a quick sync or clear list of product asks we can present to the TruMed security team tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AM — Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model affinity exemption & geo lock for TruMed pilot

Jonas — thanks for the context. High-level thoughts:

1) Model affinity vs no-fallback: We can implement a per-route "affinity" mode that prefers a pinned variant but keeps a policy-level fallback (e.g., degrade to read-only mode or return a 503) instead of silently switching to a different model. That gives us an engineering-safe posture while honoring the customer's ask for no silent substitution. If Legal insists on literal "no fallback," Ops will flag unacceptable availability risk.

2) US-only routing: Technically straightforward for Hosted and Dedicated customers via region constraints + route policy. For Private (VPC), depends on their network setup; we'd need to verify subnets and egress. Marcus: can you confirm the steps and time estimate to lock a route to US regions only?

3) Monitoring/SLA: We'll need extra telemetry: token-level model routing logs, per-route health checks, and a runbook for model variant evacuation. Ask the customer to accept a narrower SLA for pinned routes (or provide compensation/credits on incidents).

I'm ok with a short internal sync today — 30 minutes to align on asks and phrasing.

- Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model affinity exemption & geo lock for TruMed pilot

Short note on ops feasibility:

- US-region lock: We can enforce route placement via our smart router to prefer US AZs only and disable cross-region fallback. For Hosted, this is a config change + policy update; for Dedicated we must update pool assignments and reserve capacity. For Private, we'll need the customer's VPC CIDR and an egress plan — that could add 2-3 business days.

- No-fallback literal interpretation: We can support a strict policy that returns a controlled error (HTTP 503 with clear messaging) if the pinned variant is unavailable. We strongly recommend an optional manual failover pathway (ops-mediated) rather than an automatic fallback.

Effort estimates: Hosted pin + telemetry: 1 engineer, 2 days; Dedicated reserve + policy: 2 engineers, 4 days; Private consult + config: 1 engineer + 1 network engineer, 3-5 days.

I'll prepare a short ops appendix with required configs and a suggested incident flow.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model affinity exemption & geo lock for TruMed pilot

Law/legal perspective:

We shouldn't sign a blanket "no fallback" clause that prevents us from taking emergency remediation steps. Proposed contract language we can offer to TruMed:

"Customer traffic will be routed to a customer-designated model variant within the US region (\"Pinned Variant\"). Redwood will not automatically route to alternative model variants for normal load management. In the event the Pinned Variant becomes unavailable due to operational incidents or security requirements, Redwood may redirect traffic to an alternate variant or return a controlled error after making commercially reasonable efforts to notify Customer. Any automatic fallback will require prior written agreement for the pilot or will be executed only under emergency conditions as defined in Section 8."

Also recommend asking TruMed to accept a pilot-specific SLA table that reflects increased risk for pinned routes.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Sara Willoughby <sara.willoughby@trumed.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model affinity exemption & geo lock for TruMed pilot

Thanks everyone — this is helpful context. A few quick clarifications from TruMed:

- We prefer the service to return a clear error rather than silently route to a different model. We understand emergency remediation may be necessary; please include examples of what qualifies as an "emergency."
- For the pilot we can accept a reduced SLA if it is explicitly documented.
- For Private/VPC deployment we will share the VPC egress details today so Marcus can validate.

Next step: Jonas, can you send the ops appendix + the draft contract paragraph Lauren suggested? If possible, we'd like both by end of day so our security team can sign off before the pilot start next Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sara Willoughby
Head of Platform Security — TruMed Health
